claims.body: It’s the Sharks’ second game in two nights. Teams on the back end of those usually spend more time defending, so we think the Predators get more of the play than usual.

claims.head: In close vs. From distance
claims.body: The Predators get in close, but the Sharks mostly shoot from distance. Nashville is one of the league’s best for shots from in close, and San Jose is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Shots from in close tend to be more dangerous, so expect the Predators to do more of their damage around the net.

notes.text: Jonathan Marchessault is day to day (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 6 games. He is a top-six forward.

Nicolas Hague has not dressed for the last 7 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Daemon Hunt has taken his spot beside Jayden Struble. That pair has had 41% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 83:43 together, up from 29% with Hague.
Shane Wright joined from SEA on Nov 2 and has played beside Filip Forsberg and Nils Höglander.
Adam Edström has started killing penalties: on the ice for 32% of the team’s shorthanded time in 20 games, up from 1% with his old team last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 28% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the third-lowest in the league (a typical team: 42%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Igor Chernyshov is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 11 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Michael Misa has taken his spot beside Will Smith and Macklin Celebrini. That line has had 44% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 52:57 together, down from 60% with Chernyshov.
Alexander Wennberg is out (upper-body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward.
Eric Pohlkamp was added to the roster on Nov 4 and has played beside Dmitry Orlov.

stakes: The Predators go in tied for second in the Central with 27 points, the Sharks fourth in the Pacific with 20 points.

SJS.head: The Sharks face a real test
SJS.body: Even though San Jose has home-ice advantage, the Sharks are on the second night of a back-to-back. On top of that, Nashville has been out-chancing opponents lately. The Sharks can pull it off if they keep the shots coming.

NSH.head: Advantage, the Predators
NSH.body: Even though San Jose has home-ice advantage, the Sharks are on the second night of a back-to-back. On top of that, Nashville has been out-chancing opponents lately. The Sharks’ way back in is piling up shots.

story.head: Josi’s favorite opponent
paras: The Predators have won seven straight, and they’re rolling. The Sharks (9-11-2) beat Utah 6-5 in a shootout last night. The Sharks won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-2 in a shootout in Nashville on Oct 15. Going in, the Predators are second in the Central (tied for ninth in the NHL) and the Sharks fourth in the Pacific (tied for 19th).

The Predators’ record (.675) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.531), largely thanks to their goaltending. So is the Sharks’ (.455 on chances worth .389), largely thanks to their goaltending.
In their seven-game winning streak, the Predators have outscored teams 23-12, including 17-10 at 5-on-5.

The Predators keep things calm after the whistle (2nd lowest), get pinned in their own end on long shifts (31st) and give up a lot of shots (31st). Nashville has allowed 2.60 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. On the other side, the Sharks are one of the league’s most physical teams (3rd) and ice the puck a lot (32nd). They also do a lot of their shooting from distance (2nd lowest), so the Preds get in close, but them mostly shoot from distance. Put that together and expect a chippy, heavy game.

Roman Josi (2 G / 21 A / 23 P in 20 GP) leads the Predators in scoring, with a point in nine straight games against San Jose. Steven Stamkos (11 G / 10 A / 21 P in 20 GP) has a team-high eleven goals. For the Sharks, Macklin Celebrini (8 G / 16 A / 24 P in 20 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games and five goals in seven games against Nashville since 2023-24.
Juuse Saros (7-3-4 / .922 SV% in 14 GS) has been terrific for Nashville and is expected to start. Alex Nedeljkovic (3-3-1 / .895 SV% in 7 GS) is expected to go for San Jose.
